general.summary: Multiple vulnerabilities have been discovered in Oracle products, the most severe of which could allow for remote code execution. Depending on the privileges associated with the account, an attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights. Accounts configured to have fewer user rights on the system could be less impacted than those that operate with administrative user rights. Of particular concern is CVE-2026-114938, dubbed “Java4Shell,” a heap-based buffer overflow that could lead to remote code execution. Researchers attribute the flaw to the hardware-accelerated Base64 decoder in OpenJDK, while Oracle lists the affected component as the Compiler in Oracle Java SE and Oracle GraalVM for JDK. Because the Java runtime is embedded in many applications, containers, and appliances, affected software may be present in more places than organizations expect. Oracle has released updates that address this vulnerability, and organizations should prioritize identifying and updating every affected Java runtime in their environment.
general.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Oracle Products Could Allow for Remote Code Execution

general.summary: Overview On November 17, 2026, public reports described CVE-2026-114938 as a memory corruption vulnerability in Java 17 and above that could allow a remote attacker to execute code without authentication. The reported severity is Critical, with a CVSSv4 score of 9.2. These CVE-specific details remain preliminary, pending confirmation in Oracle or OpenJDK advisories. Rapid7 is actively monitoring the situation and will update this blog as new information arrives. For the latest vendor release information, refer to Oracle's November security update notice and OpenJDK's vulnerability advisories . Rapid7 customers Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose customers can assess exposure to CVE-2026-114938 with an authenticated vulnerability check available in the November 17 content release (1.1.4115).
